title: 同事不接受修改意见，怎么把分歧谈下去？

source.title: Handling pushback in code reviews
source.context: 原文讨论谷歌公开的代码评审指南，下面的练习将表达方法迁移到报告和项目讨论。
paragraphs: When a developer disagrees with your suggestion, first take a moment to consider if they are correct. Often, they are closer to the code than you are, and so they might really have a better insight about certain aspects of it. Does their argument make sense? Does it make sense from a code health perspective? If so, let them know that they are right and let the issue drop.

However, developers are not always right. In this case the reviewer should further explain why they believe that their suggestion is correct. A good explanation demonstrates both an understanding of the developer’s reply, and additional information about why the change is being requested.

In particular, when the reviewer believes their suggestion will improve code health, they should continue to advocate for the change, if they believe the resulting code quality improvement justifies the additional work requested. Improving code health tends to happen in small steps.

Sometimes it takes a few rounds of explaining a suggestion before it really sinks in. Just make sure to always stay polite and let the developer know that you hear what they’re saying, you just don’t agree.
translations: 当开发者不同意你的建议时，先花一点时间考虑他是否说得对。他通常比你更接近这段代码，因此可能对某些方面了解得更深入。他的理由说得通吗？从代码长期健康的角度看，站得住脚吗？如果是，就告诉他他是对的，并放下这个问题。
但开发者也并非总是正确。这时，评审者应该进一步解释为什么自己认为这项建议是对的。好的解释既表明你理解了对方的回复，也补充说明你为什么要求修改。
尤其当评审者认为建议有利于代码长期健康，而且带来的质量改进值得额外投入时，就应该继续为这项修改争取支持。代码质量往往是一步一步提高的。
有时，一项建议需要解释几轮才能真正被理解。始终保持礼貌，并让开发者知道：你听到了他的意见，只是仍然持不同看法。
fullTextParagraphs: Sometimes a developer will push back on a code review. Either they will disagree with your suggestion or they will complain that you are being too strict in general.

When a developer disagrees with your suggestion, first take a moment to consider if they are correct. Often, they are closer to the code than you are, and so they might really have a better insight about certain aspects of it. Does their argument make sense? Does it make sense from a code health perspective? If so, let them know that they are right and let the issue drop.

However, developers are not always right. In this case the reviewer should further explain why they believe that their suggestion is correct. A good explanation demonstrates both an understanding of the developer’s reply, and additional information about why the change is being requested.

In particular, when the reviewer believes their suggestion will improve code health, they should continue to advocate for the change, if they believe the resulting code quality improvement justifies the additional work requested. Improving code health tends to happen in small steps.

Sometimes it takes a few rounds of explaining a suggestion before it really sinks in. Just make sure to always stay polite and let the developer know that you hear what they’re saying, you just don’t agree.

Reviewers sometimes believe that the developer will be upset if the reviewer insists on an improvement. Sometimes developers do become upset, but it is usually brief and they become very thankful later that you helped them improve the quality of their code. Usually, if you are polite in your comments, developers actually don’t become upset at all, and the worry is just in the reviewer’s mind. Upsets are usually more about the way comments are written than about the reviewer’s insistence on code quality.

A common source of push back is that developers (understandably) want to get things done. They don’t want to go through another round of review just to get this CL in. So they say they will clean something up in a later CL, and thus you should LGTM this CL now. Some developers are very good about this, and will immediately write a follow-up CL that fixes the issue. However, experience shows that as more time passes after a developer writes the original CL, the less likely this clean up is to happen. In fact, usually unless the developer does the clean up immediately after the present CL, it never happens. This isn’t because developers are irresponsible, but because they have a lot of work to do and the cleanup gets lost or forgotten in the press of other work. Thus, it is usually best to insist that the developer clean up their CL now, before the code is in the codebase and “done.” Letting people “clean things up later” is a common way for codebases to degenerate.

If a CL introduces new complexity, it must be cleaned up before submission unless it is an emergency. If the CL exposes surrounding problems and they can’t be addressed right now, the developer should file a bug for the cleanup and assign it to themselves so that it doesn’t get lost. They can optionally also write a TODO comment in the code that references the filed bug.

If you previously had fairly lax code reviews and you switch to having strict reviews, some developers will complain very loudly. Improving the speed of your code reviews usually causes these complaints to fade away.

Sometimes it can take months for these complaints to fade away, but eventually developers tend to see the value of strict code reviews as they see what great code they help generate. Sometimes the loudest protesters even become your strongest supporters once something happens that causes them to really see the value you’re adding by being strict.

If you are following all of the above but you still encounter a conflict between yourself and a developer that can’t be resolved, see The Standard of Code Review for guidelines and principles that can help resolve the conflict.

notes.phrase: first take a moment to consider if they are correct
notes.meaning: 先判断对方是否有道理
notes.explain: first 放在行动前，提醒自己先检查判断，而不是立刻反驳。
notes.example: Before we reject the idea, let's consider whether it solves the customer's problem.

notes.explain: make sense 用来判断理由是否成立；这里的 argument 指论点，不是吵架。
notes.example: Your argument makes sense. I hadn't considered that constraint.

notes.phrase: let them know that they are right
notes.explain: let someone know that ... 是直接、礼貌地传达判断。
notes.example: You are right about the timeline. I missed the approval step.

notes.phrase: demonstrates both an understanding of the developer’s reply
notes.meaning: 先表明你理解对方的回复
notes.explain: demonstrate an understanding of ... 比简单说 I understand 更具体，后面还需要补上理由。
notes.example: I understand why you prefer the current approach, especially given the deadline.

notes.phrase: continue to advocate for the change
notes.explain: advocate for 表示提出理由支持某件事，并不等于强硬命令。
notes.example: I still advocate for a shorter report because the decision makers need the key points first.

notes.phrase: let the developer know that you hear what they’re saying
notes.meaning: 让对方知道他的意见被认真听见
notes.explain: I hear what you're saying 常用于承认对方观点，后面可接自己的不同判断。
notes.example: I hear what you're saying, but I still think we should test the alternative.

scenario.title: Before sending the client report
english: Maya asks Alex to move the key findings to the first page of a client report. Alex disagrees: the current order follows the team's usual template.

Maya first checks whether Alex has a good reason. The client may indeed expect the standard format. She replies, “I see why you kept the usual structure. Could we ask the account manager which version would be easier for the client to scan?”
After checking, they learn that the client wants the conclusion first. Maya explains the reason for the change, and Alex agrees to revise the opening page.
chinese: Maya 建议 Alex 把客户报告的关键发现移到第一页。Alex 不同意，因为现有顺序沿用团队常用模板。
Maya 先核对 Alex 是否有充分理由：客户也许确实期待标准格式。她说：“我明白你为什么保留常用结构。我们能否问问客户经理，哪种版本更方便客户快速浏览？”
核对后，他们得知客户希望先看到结论。Maya 说明调整的原因，Alex 同意修改首页。

firstAttempt.prompt: 同事沿用旧模板撰写客户报告，但客户明确希望先看到结论。请用英文先回应同事的考虑，再说明客户要求并提出具体调整。
firstAttempt.sample: I see why you kept the usual structure. The client asked to see the conclusion first, so could we move the key findings to page one?
firstAttempt.rationale: 先回应同事采用旧模板的原因，再引用客户要求，最后提出明确修改。

words.example: We received pushback on the new timeline.
words.translation: 新时间表遇到了反对意见。

words.example: I disagree with the proposed deadline.
words.translation: 我不同意建议的截止日期。

words.example: I still advocate for a clearer summary.
words.translation: 我仍主张写一份更清楚的摘要。
words.note: advocate for 强调提出理由支持。

words.example: The expected benefit justifies the extra work.
words.translation: 预期收益足以说明额外工作的必要性。
words.note: 常用来比较收益与成本。

words.example: We can stay polite even when we disagree.
words.translation: 即使意见不同，我们仍可以保持礼貌。
words.note: 礼貌不等于放弃自己的判断。

structure.original: A good explanation demonstrates both an understanding of the developer’s reply, and additional information about why the change is being requested.
analysis: 主语 A good explanation：什么样的解释才有效。
both ... and ...：并列两项内容——理解对方的回复、补充修改理由。
why the change is being requested：说明提出修改请求的原因。
structure.transfer: A good reply shows both that you heard the concern and why you still recommend the change.

rewrite.bad: That structure is wrong. Rewrite the report.
rewrite.good: I see why you kept the usual structure. The client asked to see the conclusion first, so could we move the key findings to page one?
rewrite.translation: 我明白你为什么保留常用结构。客户要求先看结论，所以我们能否把关键发现移到第一页？
rewrite.pattern: I see why… . [The client/team] asked to… . Could we…?

cloze.prompt: I see why you kept the usual ___.
cloze.why: 回应对方采用当前结构的原因。

cloze.prompt: The client asked to see the ___ first.
cloze.why: 用 asked to 引出客户提出的具体要求。

cloze.prompt: Could we move the key findings to page ___?
cloze.why: 用 Could we 提出具体调整。

dictation.text: I see why you kept the usual structure.
dictation.why: I see why ... 可先认可对方的理由。

translationPractice.prompt: 我明白你为什么保留常用结构。
translationPractice.answer: I see why you kept the usual structure.
translationPractice.why: 用 I see why 回应对方的考虑。

translationPractice.prompt: 我们能否把关键发现移到第一页？
translationPractice.answer: Could we move the key findings to page one?
translationPractice.why: 用 Could we 提出具体、可讨论的修改建议。

choice.prompt: 同事坚持沿用旧模板，但客户已明确要求先看结论。请用两句英文承认同事的理由、说明客户要求，并提出具体修改。
options: No, that format is wrong. Change it.
I see why you followed the usual template. The client asked to see the conclusion first, so could we move the key findings to page one?
You are wrong. Just change it.
choice.why: 先承认沿用模板的理由，再说明客户已提出的新要求并给出具体调整。

output.prompt: 设计同事坚持沿用旧版仪表盘，但销售团队反馈客户找不到关键指标。请用英文先承认旧设计的考虑，再转述客户反馈，并提出一个可共同验证的调整。
output.sample: I understand why you want to keep the current layout. Sales has heard that customers can’t find the key metrics. Could we test moving those metrics to the top with a few users before changing the full dashboard?
check: 是否承认旧版布局原本的考虑？
是否准确转述客户找不到关键指标的反馈？
是否提出先小范围验证再全面调整？
